306	Note (added in v0.3, HC2 decision, ADR-0004): a `number` input whose text the browser cannot
307	parse (for example `abc` or `1e`) reaches the form model as empty (`''`), because of the HTML
308	value sanitisation rule for `<input type="number">`. The field is then handled as empty: a
309	**required** field fails the `required` check and shows its `requiredMessage` if configured,
310	otherwise its `errorMessage` (the seed's CO "Modelo (año)" has no `requiredMessage`, so the
311	field-level message is shown); an **optional** field is treated as empty, so it is valid and
312	its output is `null` (US-01-Q-26, §7.3). The app does not show a separate "not a number"
313	message. Unit tests cover the empty-value path; the CO e2e test
314	(`us-01-data-form-co.spec.ts`) confirms the sanitisation in a real browser, because jsdom does
315	not reproduce it (SPIKE-01, *Not verified* item 1).

712	## 7. Content contract (what Strapi must provide)
713	
714	This section is **logical**. The physical model is fixed by ADR-0001 and implemented by the
715	strapi-developer following `strapi-content-modeling`: a `country` collection type (`code`
716	ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 upper case, unique; `name`; `currencyCode`; `locale`; `sortOrder`; draft &
717	publish on) and a `form-field` collection type with a **required `manyToOne` relation
718	`country`**; `documents.strictRelations: true`, so an item without a country cannot be
719	published; `key` uniqueness per country enforced by a Document Service middleware (Strapi's
720	`unique` is not scoped by relation). The front end reads one country's fields in one request
721	filtered by `country.code`, and reads only published content through the same-origin proxy
722	(ADR-0002).
723	
724	### 7.1 Field configuration (per country, draft & publish on)
725	
726	| Attribute | Type | Rules |
727	|---|---|---|
728	| `key` | string | Required. `^[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9]*$`. Unique per country. Not shown to users. |
729	| `label` | string | Required, non-empty. Spanish. |
730	| `type` | enumeration | `text`, `number`, `select`, `date`, `checkbox`. |
731	| `isRequired` | boolean | Default `false`. |
732	| `helpText` | text | Optional. Spanish. |
733	| `placeholder` | string | Optional. Spanish. Never used instead of a label. |
734	| `errorMessage` | string | Required. Spanish. Field-level message (US-01-Q-04). |
735	| `sortOrder` | integer | Required. Ascending; ties by `key`. |
736	| `options` | list of { `value` string, `label` string, `sortOrder` integer } | Required and non-empty when `type` is `select`; ignored otherwise. `value` unique within the field. |
737	| `rules` | list of structured rules (below) | Zero or more, in evaluation order. Each may carry an optional `message` (Spanish) that overrides `errorMessage`. |
738	| `requiredMessage` | string | Optional. Overrides `errorMessage` for the `required` check. |
739	| `country` | required `manyToOne` relation to `country` (ADR-0001) | Exactly one country per field. Publishing without it is rejected (`strictRelations`). |
740	
741	Rule kinds (structured, not free JSON):
742	
743	| Kind | Parameters | Applies to | Semantics |
744	|---|---|---|---|
745	| `minLength` / `maxLength` | `value` integer ≥ 0 | text | Trimmed length, inclusive. |
746	| `min` / `max` | `value` number | number | Inclusive. |
747	| `pattern` | `value` ECMAScript regex source, no flags | text | Full match (anchored if not anchored). |
748	| `minAge` | `years` integer > 0 | date | BR-04. |
749	| `yearRange` | `maxYearsOld` integer ≥ 0, `maxYearsAhead` integer ≥ 0 | number | BR-03. |
750	| `rutCheckDigit` | none | text | Modulo-11 check digit, accepts dots/dash and `K`/`k` (subject to US-01-Q-09). |
751	
752	A rule whose kind does not apply to the field's type is malformed (US-01-Q-18).

780	### 7.3 Step 1 output (consumed by US-02 and US-03 through the wizard state)
781	
782	Two shapes exist (ADR-0003, HC2 decision). Only the second one is consumed by US-02 and US-03.
783	
784	**Stored editing values** (written on every change; what a reload restores):
785	
786	- `country`: the country code of the context (see below).
787	- `values`: a map from field `key` to the **raw editing value** of the form model, as typed:
788	  a string for `text`, `number`, `select` and `date`, a boolean for `checkbox`, and `''` for an
789	  empty field. In-progress invalid values (for example `'2015.5'`) are stored as typed. The model
790	  never holds `null` (ADR-0004).
791	
792	**Typed step 1 output** (produced only on a valid "Continuar"; never on an invalid one):
793	
794	- `country`: an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code in upper case (`^[A-Z]{2}$`) that matches a published
795	  `country` entry loaded from Strapi in this page load (ADR-0001). `CO` and `CL` are the seeded
796	  values; the type is not a fixed union of them.
797	- `values`: a map from field `key` to value. `text` → trimmed string; `number` → integer;
798	  `select` → option `value`; `date` → ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` string. An empty **optional** `text`,
799	  `number`, `select` or `date` field → `null`. `checkbox` → always a boolean: checked → `true`,
800	  unchecked → `false`, also when the checkbox is optional (HC2 decision); a checkbox is never
801	  `null`.
802	- The field configuration is **not** stored: later steps read labels and option labels from the
803	  configuration fetched in the same page load (refetched on every full page load, ADR-0003,
804	  US-01-Q-16).
805	- Reserved keys (US-01-Q-08): `documentType` (CO only), `documentNumber`, `fullName`,
806	  `birthDate`, `plate`, `make`, `model`, `vehicleYear`.
807	
808	### 7.4 Differences from the `dynamic-form-fields` skill contract v0
809	
810	The skill says the US-01 spec may refine the contract and that the skill is updated in the same
811	PR. Differences proposed here:
812	
813	1. A required field-level `errorMessage` plus optional per-rule overrides (`requiredMessage`,
814	   rule `message`), instead of only a per-rule-kind `messages` map (US-01-Q-04).
815	2. A new rule kind `rutCheckDigit` (US-01-Q-09).
816	3. `number` fields are integers only (US-01-Q-12).
817	4. Empty optional fields skip all rules (US-01-Q-26). The skill does not state this.
818	5. Rules carry an applicability by field type (§7.1); a mismatch is malformed.

836	## 9. Non-functional requirements
837	
838	- **Accessibility (Assessment):** the step can be completed with the keyboard only (AC-24), and
839	  every field has an accessible label (AC-25). Native controls are used (`input` of type text,
840	  number, date and checkbox; `select`). Visible focus indicator. Errors are associated with their
841	  field and announced once. Target: WCAG 2.2 AA for step 1 (verified in part automatically and in
842	  part by hand at HC3, including one screen reader pass).
843	- **Responsive (Assessment):** usable from 320 to 1440 CSS px wide without horizontal scroll;
844	  verified by hand at HC3 at 360 × 740 and 1280 × 800, with screenshots as evidence (AC-26); one
845	  column; touch targets at least 24 × 24 CSS px.
846	- **Multi-country (Assessment):** one build for CO and CL; no country-specific code paths for
847	  fields or copy (BR-07).
848	- **Content-driven (Assessment, BR-06):** every field-related string, option, rule and the order
849	  come from Strapi. No field list is hard-coded in the front end.
850	- **Typed validations (Assessment):** the configuration is parsed at the boundary into a typed
851	  model (§7.1) before it reaches the form; validators are pure functions with an injectable clock.
852	- **Security / privacy (Assessment, CLAUDE.md §3):** no Strapi token with write permissions
853	  reaches the browser; the browser only reads content (AC-27). Public role permissions are
854	  minimal and justified in ADR-0002 (`find` on `country` and `form-field` only); anonymous reads
855	  return published content only, and the browser reaches the content API only through the
856	  same-origin, GET-only proxy at the relative `/api` (ADR-0002, AC-28). Step 1 values are never sent to a server or written
857	  to logs; console warnings contain no user data. Seed and test data are fictitious.
858	- **Performance:** the configuration of a country is loaded with as few requests as the content
859	  model allows (target: one), with options and rules populated in the same response. No request
860	  per keystroke. Validation runs on the client.
861	- **Environment (Assessment):** the stack starts with a single command (for example
862	  `docker compose up`) with the seed for both countries.
863	- **Language:** all end-user copy is Spanish; code, logs and docs are English.

Verification: manual, by the human at HC3, with evidence: one screenshot of step 1 of Colombia
at 360 × 740 and one at 1280 × 800, attached to the HC3 record. "Reach step 2" means the address
changes to the step 2 route (US-01-Q-27). No automated test is planned for this AC.

### US-01-AC-27 — Read-only content access, data stays in the browser (derived from US-01-BR-08 / Assessment: security)

```gherkin
Scenario: Read-only content access, data stays in the browser
  Given I complete step 1 in the context of Colombia with the values of US-01-AC-04 and reach step 2
  When I inspect every network request made by the browser during the flow
  Then every request to the content backend is a read (HTTP GET)
  And no request carries a Strapi API token with write permissions
  And no request contains any value I entered in step 1
```

"Reach step 2" means that a valid "Continuar" leads to the step 2 address (US-01-Q-27). The
requests are inspected from the first page load until that navigation.

### US-01-AC-28 — Anonymous callers cannot read drafts or write content (derived from US-01-BR-06 / ADR-0002)

New in v0.3 (HC2 decision: the ADR-0002 security check is traced as an AC).

```gherkin
Scenario Outline: Anonymous requests never return draft content
  Given the seed field "Correo electrónico" (key "email") exists for Colombia only as a draft
  When an anonymous client, without any token, requests the Colombia form fields with
    "status=draft" and "filters[key][$eq]=email" through <entry point>
  Then the response contains no field with key "email"

  Examples:
    | entry point                                 |
    | Strapi's own port (bypassing the proxy)     |
    | the same-origin proxy at the relative "/api" |

Scenario: Writes through the same-origin proxy are rejected
  When an anonymous client sends "POST /api/form-fields" through the same-origin proxy, with a
    Colombia field of key "securityProbe", type "text", label "Prueba"
  Then the response status is 405
  And an anonymous read of the Colombia form fields returns no field with key "securityProbe"
```

Verification: e2e file `us-01-security.spec.ts`, as API requests from the Playwright Node
process with no browser and no token (ADR-0002 *Confirmation*). The
check is re-run on every Strapi upgrade (ADR-0002, *Strongest argument against*).

## 6. Gaps and open questions

Gaps marked **[Blocks HC1]** change the ACs or a contract shared with other stories, so they need
an explicit answer. For the others, the proposed default applies if the human does not answer.

| ID | Gap | Why it matters | Proposed default | Human answer |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| US-01-Q-01 | **[Blocks HC1] [ADR]** "Open the application in the context of a country": how is the country resolved (URL path, query parameter, subdomain, selector, browser locale)? What happens with no country or an unsupported one? | AC-01, AC-17 and every e2e test depend on it. The same build must serve both countries (Assessment). | Decided by the multi-country ADR. Proposal to evaluate: a country segment in the URL (`/co/…`, `/cl/…`), so it can be deep-linked, bookmarked and tested. The root address shows a country chooser (links "Colombia", "Chile"). An unsupported code shows "Este país no está disponible." with the same links (AC-17). No detection from IP or browser locale. | Decided by the ADR. The proposal (/co, /cl, chooser at the root, message "Este país no está disponible.") is the starting point. — Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-20 (HC1) |
| US-01-Q-02 | Can the user switch country mid-flow, and what happens to the data already entered? | Fields differ by country; values from CO are meaningless in CL. Privacy. | Switching is possible only by opening the other country's context (no in-page selector in US-01). The wizard state is scoped to one country: opening another country's context discards the stored data of the previous one (AC-22). | Default accepted. — Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-20 (HC1) |
| US-01-Q-03 | **[Blocks HC1]** The story names some fields (document, plate, make, city, birth date implied by legal age, vehicle year) but not the complete list, labels, copy, options or patterns per country. | The seed, the e2e tests and the downstream stories (US-02 price rule, US-03 summary) depend on concrete fields. | The seed in §7.2: 10 fields for CO and 9 for CL, all five field types used, Spanish copy as written there, fictitious options. Editors can change all of it later. | OK. — Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-20 (HC1) |
| US-01-Q-04 | **[Blocks HC1]** The story says each field has *an* error message (singular), but a field can fail for different reasons (empty vs. wrong format). Can messages contain dynamic values (for example the allowed year range)? | Defines the content model and AC-02/AC-09. A single message per field makes "required" and "wrong format" read the same. | Each field has a required field-level `errorMessage`, plus an optional message per rule (including `required`) that overrides it for that rule. ## 7. Content contract (what Strapi must provide)

This section is **logical**. The physical model is fixed by ADR-0001 and implemented by the
strapi-developer following `strapi-content-modeling`: a `country` collection type (`code`
ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 upper case, unique; `name`; `currencyCode`; `locale`; `sortOrder`; draft &
publish on) and a `form-field` collection type with a **required `manyToOne` relation
`country`**; `documents.strictRelations: true`, so an item without a country cannot be
published; `key` uniqueness per country enforced by a Document Service middleware (Strapi's
`unique` is not scoped by relation). The front end reads one country's fields in one request
filtered by `country.code`, and reads only published content through the same-origin proxy
(ADR-0002).

### 7.1 Field configuration (per country, draft & publish on)

| Attribute | Type | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | string | Required. `^[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9]*$`. Unique per country. Not shown to users. |
| `label` | string | Required, non-empty. Spanish. |
| `type` | enumeration | `text`, `number`, `select`, `date`, `checkbox`. |
| `isRequired` | boolean | Default `false`. |
| `helpText` | text | Optional. Spanish. |
| `placeholder` | string | Optional. Spanish. Never used instead of a label. |
| `errorMessage` | string | Required. Spanish. Field-level message (US-01-Q-04). |
| `sortOrder` | integer | Required. Ascending; ties by `key`. |
| `options` | list of { `value` string, `label` string, `sortOrder` integer } | Required and non-empty when `type` is `select`; ignored otherwise. `value` unique within the field. |
| `rules` | list of structured rules (below) | Zero or more, in evaluation order. Each may carry an optional `message` (Spanish) that overrides `errorMessage`. |
| `requiredMessage` | string | Optional. Overrides `errorMessage` for the `required` check. |
| `country` | required `manyToOne` relation to `country` (ADR-0001) | Exactly one country per field. Publishing without it is rejected (`strictRelations`). |

Rule kinds (structured, not free JSON):

| Kind | Parameters | Applies to | Semantics |
|---|---|---|---|
| `minLength` / `maxLength` | `value` integer ≥ 0 | text | Trimmed length, inclusive. |
| `min` / `max` | `value` number | number | Inclusive. |
| `pattern` | `value` ECMAScript regex source, no flags | text | Full match (anchored if not anchored). |
| `minAge` | `years` integer > 0 | date | BR-04. |
| `yearRange` | `maxYearsOld` integer ≥ 0, `maxYearsAhead` integer ≥ 0 | number | BR-03. |
| `rutCheckDigit` | none | text | Modulo-11 check digit, accepts dots/dash and `K`/`k` (subject to US-01-Q-09). |

A rule whose kind does not apply to the field's type is malformed (US-01-Q-18).

### 7.3 Step 1 output (consumed by US-02 and US-03 through the wizard state)

Two shapes exist (ADR-0003, HC2 decision). Only the second one is consumed by US-02 and US-03.

**Stored editing values** (written on every change; what a reload restores):

- `country`: the country code of the context (see below).
- `values`: a map from field `key` to the **raw editing value** of the form model, as typed:
  a string for `text`, `number`, `select` and `date`, a boolean for `checkbox`, and `''` for an
  empty field. In-progress invalid values (for example `'2015.5'`) are stored as typed. The model
  never holds `null` (ADR-0004).

**Typed step 1 output** (produced only on a valid "Continuar"; never on an invalid one):

- `country`: an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code in upper case (`^[A-Z]{2}$`) that matches a published
  `country` entry loaded from Strapi in this page load (ADR-0001). `CO` and `CL` are the seeded
  values; the type is not a fixed union of them.
- `values`: a map from field `key` to value. `text` → trimmed string; `number` → integer;
  `select` → option `value`; `date` → ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` string. An empty **optional** `text`,
  `number`, `select` or `date` field → `null`. `checkbox` → always a boolean: checked → `true`,
  unchecked → `false`, also when the checkbox is optional (HC2 decision); a checkbox is never
  `null`.
- The field configuration is **not** stored: later steps read labels and option labels from the
  configuration fetched in the same page load (refetched on every full page load, ADR-0003,
  US-01-Q-16).
- Reserved keys (US-01-Q-08): `documentType` (CO only), `documentNumber`, `fullName`,
  `birthDate`, `plate`, `make`, `model`, `vehicleYear`.

### 7.4 Differences from the `dynamic-form-fields` skill contract v0

The skill says the US-01 spec may refine the contract and that the skill is updated in the same
PR. Differences proposed here:

1. A required field-level `errorMessage` plus optional per-rule overrides (`requiredMessage`,
   rule `message`), instead of only a per-rule-kind `messages` map (US-01-Q-04).
2. A new rule kind `rutCheckDigit` (US-01-Q-09).
3. `number` fields are integers only (US-01-Q-12).
4. Empty optional fields skip all rules (US-01-Q-26). The skill does not state this.
5. Rules carry an applicability by field type (§7.1); a mismatch is malformed.

## 9. Non-functional requirements

- **Accessibility (Assessment):** the step can be completed with the keyboard only (AC-24), and
  every field has an accessible label (AC-25). Native controls are used (`input` of type text,
  number, date and checkbox; `select`). Visible focus indicator. Errors are associated with their
  field and announced once. Target: WCAG 2.2 AA for step 1 (verified in part automatically and in
  part by hand at HC3, including one screen reader pass).
- **Responsive (Assessment):** usable from 320 to 1440 CSS px wide without horizontal scroll;
  verified by hand at HC3 at 360 × 740 and 1280 × 800, with screenshots as evidence (AC-26); one
  column; touch targets at least 24 × 24 CSS px.
- **Multi-country (Assessment):** one build for CO and CL; no country-specific code paths for
  fields or copy (BR-07).
- **Content-driven (Assessment, BR-06):** every field-related string, option, rule and the order
  come from Strapi. No field list is hard-coded in the front end.
- **Typed validations (Assessment):** the configuration is parsed at the boundary into a typed
  model (§7.1) before it reaches the form; validators are pure functions with an injectable clock.
- **Security / privacy (Assessment, CLAUDE.md §3):** no Strapi token with write permissions
  reaches the browser; the browser only reads content (AC-27). Public role permissions are
  minimal and justified in ADR-0002 (`find` on `country` and `form-field` only); anonymous reads
  return published content only, and the browser reaches the content API only through the
  same-origin, GET-only proxy at the relative `/api` (ADR-0002, AC-28). Step 1 values are never sent to a server or written
  to logs; console warnings contain no user data. Seed and test data are fictitious.
- **Performance:** the configuration of a country is loaded with as few requests as the content
  model allows (target: one), with options and rules populated in the same response. No request
  per keystroke. Validation runs on the client.
- **Environment (Assessment):** the stack starts with a single command (for example
  `docker compose up`) with the seed for both countries.
- **Language:** all end-user copy is Spanish; code, logs and docs are English.

# ADR-0001: Multi-country content strategy and country context

## Context and Problem Statement

One Angular build serves Colombia and Chile, and every piece of content the wizard shows (form
fields in US-01, plans in US-02, terms and conditions in US-03) differs by country and is edited
by a non-technical business team in Strapi. We must decide (1) how Strapi models which country an
item belongs to and where country-level metadata (currency, number locale) lives, and (2) how the
Angular app knows which country it is running for, including the root address, unknown
countries, switching country (US-01-Q-01, US-01-Q-02) and, folded into this ADR, the wizard step
addresses and the step 2 guard (spec §10 candidate, US-01-Q-19, US-01-Q-27).

## Decision Drivers

- D1. "The same application and the same build serve Colombia and Chile." (source: Assessment; US-01-BR-07)
- D2. "Content differentiation strategy by country, proposed by you and documented in an ADR" (source: Assessment, multi-country)
- D3. "Content differentiated by country without duplicating the app; form and plans 100% configurable from Strapi" (source: Assessment, evaluation); "The business team, which is not technical, must be able to change the form fields and the offered plans from Strapi without requesting a deployment." (source: Assessment, business context)
- D4. "Each country has its own regulations, identity documents, currency, coverages and copy" (source: Assessment, business context). Currency and number format need a per-country home (US-02 story: "The price is shown in the country's currency and format").
- D5. Per-item draft & publish: a single field can be a draft while the rest is published (US-01-AC-13, US-01-Q-24); plans need "published and active" per item (US-02 story).
- D6. The country context must be deep-linkable and testable; root chooser and "Este país no está disponible." (US-01-Q-01 human answer, US-01-AC-17); data never crosses countries (US-01-BR-07, US-01-AC-22).
- D7. Field `key` unique per country (US-01-BR-01, spec §7.1); one request per country configuration (spec §9, performance).
- D8. Step 2 route exists with the AC-19 guard and no page of its own; browser back works per step (US-01-Q-27, US-01-Q-20, US-01-AC-19, US-01-AC-20).
- D9. Public permissions minimal (source: Assessment, security). The model must not force broad read permissions.

## Considered Options

Strapi model (the four options from the `strapi-content-modeling` skill):

1. **A. `country` collection type + `manyToOne` relation** on every per-country type.
2. **B. i18n locales as countries** (`es-CO`, `es-CL`).
3. **C. Enumeration attribute `country`** (`CO`, `CL`) on every per-country type.
4. **D. One document per country** (a `country-config` holding fields and plans as components or dynamic zones).

Country resolution in Angular:

- **R1. Path segment** `/co/…`, `/cl/…`, chooser at `/`.
- **R2. Host name** (`co.example.test`, `cl.example.test`).
- **R3. Query parameter** (`?pais=co`).
- **R4. In-app selector** with the choice kept in storage, no country in the URL.

## Decision Outcome

Chosen option: **"A. `country` collection type + relation" with "R1. Path segment"**, because A
is the only model that gives every item its own draft/publish lifecycle (D5) *and* a typed home for
country metadata (D4) without a schema change per country (D3), and R1 makes the country context
explicit, deep-linkable and testable with one build (D1, D6) without DNS or hosts-file setup.

### What is decided

**Strapi model**

- A `country` collection type (API ID `country`, draft & publish on) with: `code` (string,
  required, unique, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 in upper case, `^[A-Z]{2}$`), `name` (Spanish, shown in the
  chooser: "Colombia", "Chile"), `currencyCode` (ISO 4217: `COP`, `CLP`), `locale` (BCP 47 tag used
  for number and currency formatting: `es-CO`, `es-CL`) and `sortOrder` (integer). Later stories
  may add country-level attributes (for example a document masking rule for US-03) through their
  own spec; this ADR fixes only where they live.
- Every per-country content type (`form-field` in US-01; `plan` in US-02; `terms` in US-03) has a
  **required `manyToOne` relation `country`** to `country`. Draft & publish is on for all of them.
- `config/api.ts` sets `documents.strictRelations: true`, so Strapi rejects publishing an item
  whose required `country` relation is empty. Verified in `@strapi/core@5.63.0`
  (`services/document-service/entries.js`, `services/entity-validator/index.js`): required
  relations are enforced only when this flag is `true`, and never for drafts.
- `key` uniqueness **per country** is enforced server-side by a Document Service middleware
  (`strapi.documents.use`, present in `@strapi/core@5.63.0`) or a lifecycle check on
  create/update/publish of `form-field`. Strapi's `unique` is not scoped by relation, so it cannot
  be used for this.
- The front end reads a country's fields in one request:
  `GET /api/form-fields?filters[country][code][$eq]=CO&populate[…]&sort=sortOrder:asc&pagination[pageSize]=100`
  (exact `populate` per the US-01 content type). Filtering through the relation needs `find` on
  `country` for the reader (verified: `@strapi/utils@5.63.0`
  `validate/visitors/throw-restricted-relations.js` checks `<target>.find` for relations used in
  filters). That permission is needed anyway for the chooser and is justified in ADR-0002.

**Country context in Angular**

- The **list of supported countries is content**: the published `country` entries, loaded once
  per full page load (`GET /api/countries?sort=sortOrder:asc`, narrow `fields[]`) into a
  `CountryStore`, validated at the boundary (`code` matches `^[A-Z]{2}$`, `name` non-empty,
  `currencyCode` matches `^[A-Z]{3}$`; invalid entries dropped with a `console.warn`). No country
  code, name or list exists in front-end code.
- The URL segment is the lower-case country code. Matching is case-insensitive; a non-canonical
  address (`/CO/datos`) redirects to the canonical lower-case one with `replaceUrl`.
- **Unknown or unpublished country** (`/ar/…`): the page shows the code-owned message "Este país
  no está disponible." and links to each loaded country (AC-17). No field configuration is
  requested. The address is kept as typed (no redirect), so the user sees what they asked for.
- **Root `/`**: country chooser listing the loaded countries as links ("Colombia", "Chile") to
  `/<code>/datos`. No detection from IP or browser locale.
- **Country list cannot be loaded** (Strapi down, timeout): the chooser and the unknown-country
  page show the same load error state as step 1 ("No pudimos cargar el formulario. Intenta de
  nuevo." is form-specific, so the copy for this state is set by the spec; see *Spec impact*) with
  "Reintentar". The app never claims a country is unavailable when it simply could not check.
- **Switching country (US-01-Q-02)**: there is no in-page selector. Switching means opening the
  other country's address (from the chooser or by typing it). Entering a supported country's
  context whose code differs from the country held in the wizard state discards the stored state
  (mechanics in ADR-0003). Visiting `/` or an unknown country does not discard anything.

**Wizard routes and step guards (folded in from the spec §10 candidate)**

| Address | Route content | Guard | Story |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/` | Country chooser page | — | US-01 |
| `/:country` | Parent route of the wizard; `canMatch: [supportedCountryGuard]` | country must be in `CountryStore` | US-01 |
| `/:country` (empty child) | `redirectTo: 'datos'` | — | US-01 |
| `/:country/datos` | Step 1 page (`QuoteFormPage`) | — | US-01 |
| `/:country/planes` | **No component** in US-01: `children: []` | `canActivate: [wizardStepGuard]` | US-01 registers it; US-02 attaches its page without changing address or guard (US-01-Q-27) |
| `/:country/resumen` | Step 3 page | guard for step 3 (defined by US-03) | US-03 |
| `/:country/**` | `redirectTo: 'datos'` | — | US-01 |
| `**` (no supported country matched) | Unknown-country page | — | US-01 |

- Step slugs are Spanish because they are user-visible (same status as the wizard chrome copy in
  US-01-Q-14); identifiers in code stay English.
- A route with `children: []` and no component is valid in `@angular/router@22.3.0`
  (`_router-chunk.mjs`, route validation error 4014 requires one of `component`,
  `loadComponent`, `redirectTo`, `children` or `loadChildren`). `redirectTo` cannot be combined
  with `canActivate`/`canMatch` on the same route (same file), which is why the redirects are
  separate child routes.
- `wizardStepGuard` is a `CanActivateFn` (`@angular/router@22.3.0`: `type CanActivateFn = (route,
  state) => MaybeAsync<GuardResult>`, `GuardResult = boolean | UrlTree | RedirectCommand`). It
  allows step 2 only if the wizard state holds step 1 values **for the route's country** that pass
  the same pure validators against the field configuration loaded in this page load. Otherwise it
  returns `new RedirectCommand(router.parseUrl('/<country>/datos'), { replaceUrl: true })`, so the
  blocked address does not stay in the history (AC-19). If the configuration cannot be loaded, it
  redirects to step 1, which shows the load error state.
- Each step is its own history entry: "Continuar" navigates normally (no `replaceUrl`), so the
  browser back action returns to step 1 (US-01-Q-20, AC-20).
- Focus on step change: the arriving step's heading receives focus (step 1 in US-01; step 2 and 3
  in their stories, spec §8).
- Field configuration and countries are fetched once per full page load and kept in memory for
  that page load only (US-01-Q-16); nothing about content is stored across reloads (ADR-0003).

### Consequences

- Good, because every field, plan and term has its own draft/publish state, ordering and audit
  history in the Strapi admin (D5), and the seed's draft-only `email` field (AC-13) is expressible.
- Good, because currency and number locale have one typed home that US-02 and US-03 reuse (D4).
- Good, because adding a third country is content work (a `country` entry plus its fields, plans
  and terms) with no schema change and no front-end change (D3), unless that country needs new
  code-backed rules.
- Good, because the URL carries the country: deep links, bookmarks, e2e tests and the AC-19 guard
  all work from the address alone (D6, D8).
- Bad, because editors must pick the country on every item; an item saved without one is invalid
  — mitigation: required relation + `strictRelations: true` blocks publishing it, and the
  frontend only queries filtered by country, so an orphan is never shown.
- Bad, because `key` uniqueness per country needs custom server code (Strapi `unique` is global) —
  mitigation: one Document Service middleware with a unit or integration test; the front end also
  drops duplicates at the boundary (AC-14).

  another locale") — mitigation: acceptable for two countries; the seed creates both.
- Bad, because the chooser and the unknown-country page now depend on Strapi being reachable —
  mitigation: they show a load error with "Reintentar" instead of a wrong "not available".
- Bad, because the public role needs `find` on `country` in addition to `form-field` — mitigation:
  `country` holds only public, non-sensitive metadata; justified in ADR-0002.
- Neutral: the step 2 address exists in US-01 with an empty content area until US-02 (accepted at
  HC1, US-01-Q-27).

### Strongest argument against

scopes its `unique` check by locale (verified in `@strapi/core@5.63.0`), and the admin lets

list would not.

in `@strapi/i18n@5.63.0`), so one wrong checkbox on a price silently overwrites the other

metadata (D3, D4). The uniqueness middleware is one small, tested piece, the front end also drops

surfaced as a load error with "Reintentar", never as a wrong "not available".

### Confirmation

- E2E `us-01-country-context.spec.ts`: CL fields only in `/cl/datos` (AC-01), `/ar/datos` shows
  the message and both links and makes no `form-fields` request (AC-17), no data across countries
  (AC-22).
- Unit tests: `supported-country-guard.spec.ts` (code matching, case normalisation, unknown code,
  list not loaded) and `wizard-step-guard.spec.ts` (AC-19: no or invalid data → `RedirectCommand`
  to `/<country>/datos` with `replaceUrl`; valid data → `true`; data of another country → redirect).
- Review checklist: no country code, country name or field list literal in `frontend/src`
  (`grep -rnE "'(CO|CL)'" frontend/src` returns only tests and fixtures); every per-country content
  type has a required `country` relation; `config/api.ts` has `strictRelations: true`.
- Seed check: restarting Strapi does not duplicate countries (natural key `code`).

## Pros and Cons of the Options

### A. `country` collection type + relation

- Good, because per-item draft & publish, ordering and filtering (`filters[country][code][$eq]`).
- Good, because country metadata (currency, locale) is a typed, editable entry.
- Good, because "market" and "language" stay separate concepts.
- Bad, because the relation must be set on each item and enforced (`strictRelations`).
- Bad, because per-country uniqueness of `key` needs custom code.

  `services/entity-validator/validators.js`: the unique query adds `locale`), so `key` is unique
  per country with no custom code.
- Good, because the admin can fill one locale from another (copy CO to CL).
- Bad, because non-localised attributes are **copied to every locale** on save (verified:
  `@strapi/i18n@5.63.0` `services/localizations.js` `syncNonLocalizedAttributes`, called from
  `bootstrap.js`). One wrong "localised" checkbox on `basePrice` and a CO edit overwrites the CL
  price.
- Bad, because it mixes language with market: a country with two languages, or English copy for
  a market, collides with the one-locale-per-country mapping.
- Bad, because there is no natural home for country metadata (currency) other than a separate
  localised single type, so a second mechanism is needed anyway.

- Good, because it is the simplest schema and filter (`filters[country][$eq]=CO`).
- Bad, because adding a country is a schema change, that is, code and a deployment (against D3).
- Bad, because there is no place for currency or locale; they would end up in front-end code,
  which BR-07 forbids.

### D. One document per country (`country-config` with components)

- Good, because one request returns everything for a country.
- Bad, because draft & publish applies to the whole document: one field cannot stay a draft while
  the others are published (breaks AC-13 and the "published and active" plan rule of US-02
  without an extra flag).
- Bad, because reordering, auditing and editing a single field means editing a large document;
  error-prone for non-technical editors.

### R1. Path segment (chosen)

- Good, because deep links, bookmarks and tests address a country directly; works on `localhost`.
- Good, because the guard and the unknown-country state derive from the URL only.
- Bad, because a user can type another country's address; mitigated by Q-02 (switching discards
  the other country's data).

### R2. Host name

- Good, because it looks natural for country sites.
- Bad, because local `docker compose up` would need hosts-file or wildcard DNS setup, against the
  single-command start (Assessment, environment).

### R3. Query parameter

- Good, because it needs no routing change.
- Bad, because it must be propagated on every navigation and is easily lost; it is a weaker key
  for guards and tests.

### R4. In-app selector stored in the browser

- Good, because URLs stay short.
- Bad, because the country is invisible and not linkable; e2e tests must drive the selector; a
  stored choice silently decides which content a user sees.

2. Spec §8 has no state for "country list could not be loaded" on the chooser and the
   unknown-country page; its copy needs to be chosen (US-01-Q-14 owns chrome copy).

# ADR-0001: Multi-country content strategy and country context

## Context and Problem Statement

One Angular build serves Colombia and Chile, and every piece of content the wizard shows (form
fields in US-01, plans in US-02, terms and conditions in US-03) differs by country and is edited
by a non-technical business team in Strapi. We must decide (1) how Strapi models which country an
item belongs to and where country-level metadata (currency, number locale) lives, and (2) how the
Angular app knows which country it is running for, including the root address, unknown
countries, switching country (US-01-Q-01, US-01-Q-02) and, folded into this ADR, the wizard step
addresses and the step 2 guard (spec §10 candidate, US-01-Q-19, US-01-Q-27).

## Decision Drivers

- D1. "The same application and the same build serve Colombia and Chile." (source: Assessment; US-01-BR-07)
- D2. "Content differentiation strategy by country, proposed by you and documented in an ADR" (source: Assessment, multi-country)
- D3. "Content differentiated by country without duplicating the app; form and plans 100% configurable from Strapi" (source: Assessment, evaluation); "The business team, which is not technical, must be able to change the form fields and the offered plans from Strapi without requesting a deployment." (source: Assessment, business context)
- D4. "Each country has its own regulations, identity documents, currency, coverages and copy" (source: Assessment, business context). Currency and number format need a per-country home (US-02 story: "The price is shown in the country's currency and format").
- D5. Per-item draft & publish: a single field can be a draft while the rest is published (US-01-AC-13, US-01-Q-24); plans need "published and active" per item (US-02 story).
- D6. The country context must be deep-linkable and testable; root chooser and "Este país no está disponible." (US-01-Q-01 human answer, US-01-AC-17); data never crosses countries (US-01-BR-07, US-01-AC-22).
- D7. Field `key` unique per country (US-01-BR-01, spec §7.1); one request per country configuration (spec §9, performance).
- D8. Step 2 route exists with the AC-19 guard and no page of its own; browser back works per step (US-01-Q-27, US-01-Q-20, US-01-AC-19, US-01-AC-20).
- D9. Public permissions minimal (source: Assessment, security). The model must not force broad read permissions.

## Considered Options

Strapi model (the four options from the `strapi-content-modeling` skill):

1. **A. `country` collection type + `manyToOne` relation** on every per-country type.
2. **B. i18n locales as countries** (`es-CO`, `es-CL`).
3. **C. Enumeration attribute `country`** (`CO`, `CL`) on every per-country type.
4. **D. One document per country** (a `country-config` holding fields and plans as components or dynamic zones).

Country resolution in Angular:

- **R1. Path segment** `/co/…`, `/cl/…`, chooser at `/`.
- **R2. Host name** (`co.example.test`, `cl.example.test`).
- **R3. Query parameter** (`?pais=co`).
- **R4. In-app selector** with the choice kept in storage, no country in the URL.

## Decision Outcome

Chosen option: **"A. `country` collection type + relation" with "R1. Path segment"**, because A
is the only model that gives every item its own draft/publish lifecycle (D5) *and* a typed home for
country metadata (D4) without a schema change per country (D3), and R1 makes the country context
explicit, deep-linkable and testable with one build (D1, D6) without DNS or hosts-file setup.

### What is decided

**Strapi model**

- A `country` collection type (API ID `country`, draft & publish on) with: `code` (string,
  required, unique, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 in upper case, `^[A-Z]{2}$`), `name` (Spanish, shown in the
  chooser: "Colombia", "Chile"), `currencyCode` (ISO 4217: `COP`, `CLP`), `locale` (BCP 47 tag used
  for number and currency formatting: `es-CO`, `es-CL`) and `sortOrder` (integer). Later stories
  may add country-level attributes (for example a document masking rule for US-03) through their
  own spec; this ADR fixes only where they live.
- Every per-country content type (`form-field` in US-01; `plan` in US-02; `terms` in US-03) has a
  **required `manyToOne` relation `country`** to `country`. Draft & publish is on for all of them.
- `config/api.ts` sets `documents.strictRelations: true`, so Strapi rejects publishing an item
  whose required `country` relation is empty. Verified in `@strapi/core@5.63.0`
  (`services/document-service/entries.js`, `services/entity-validator/index.js`): required
  relations are enforced only when this flag is `true`, and never for drafts.
- `key` uniqueness **per country** is enforced server-side by a Document Service middleware
  (`strapi.documents.use`, present in `@strapi/core@5.63.0`) or a lifecycle check on
  create/update/publish of `form-field`. Strapi's `unique` is not scoped by relation, so it cannot
  be used for this.
- The front end reads a country's fields in one request:
  `GET /api/form-fields?filters[country][code][$eq]=CO&populate[…]&sort=sortOrder:asc&pagination[pageSize]=100`

  `country` for the reader (verified: `@strapi/utils@5.63.0`

- The **list of supported countries is content**: the published `country` entries, loaded once
  per full page load (`GET /api/countries?sort=sortOrder:asc`, narrow `fields[]`) into a
  `CountryStore`, validated at the boundary (`code` matches `^[A-Z]{2}$`, `name` non-empty,
  `currencyCode` matches `^[A-Z]{3}$`; invalid entries dropped with a `console.warn`). No country
  code, name or list exists in front-end code.
- The URL segment is the lower-case country code. Matching is case-insensitive; a non-canonical
  address (`/CO/datos`) redirects to the canonical lower-case one with `replaceUrl`.
- **Unknown or unpublished country** (`/ar/…`): the page shows the code-owned message "Este país
  no está disponible." and links to each loaded country (AC-17). No field configuration is
  requested. The address is kept as typed (no redirect), so the user sees what they asked for.
- **Root `/`**: country chooser listing the loaded countries as links ("Colombia", "Chile") to
  `/<code>/datos`. No detection from IP or browser locale.
- **Country list cannot be loaded** (Strapi down, timeout): the chooser and the unknown-country
  page show the same load error state as step 1 ("No pudimos cargar el formulario. Intenta de
  nuevo." is form-specific, so the copy for this state is set by the spec; see *Spec impact*) with
  "Reintentar". The app never claims a country is unavailable when it simply could not check.
- **Switching country (US-01-Q-02)**: there is no in-page selector. Switching means opening the
  other country's address (from the chooser or by typing it). Entering a supported country's
  context whose code differs from the country held in the wizard state discards the stored state
  (mechanics in ADR-0003). Visiting `/` or an unknown country does not discard anything.

**Wizard routes and step guards (folded in from the spec §10 candidate)**

| Address | Route content | Guard | Story |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/` | Country chooser page | — | US-01 |
| `/:country` | Parent route of the wizard; `canMatch: [supportedCountryGuard]` | country must be in `CountryStore` | US-01 |
| `/:country` (empty child) | `redirectTo: 'datos'` | — | US-01 |
| `/:country/datos` | Step 1 page (`QuoteFormPage`) | — | US-01 |
| `/:country/planes` | **No component** in US-01: `children: []` | `canActivate: [wizardStepGuard]` | US-01 registers it; US-02 attaches its page without changing address or guard (US-01-Q-27) |
| `/:country/resumen` | Step 3 page | guard for step 3 (defined by US-03) | US-03 |
| `/:country/**` | `redirectTo: 'datos'` | — | US-01 |
| `**` (no supported country matched) | Unknown-country page | — | US-01 |

- Step slugs are Spanish because they are user-visible (same status as the wizard chrome copy in
  US-01-Q-14); identifiers in code stay English.
- A route with `children: []` and no component is valid in `@angular/router@22.3.0`
  (`_router-chunk.mjs`, route validation error 4014 requires one of `component`,
  `loadComponent`, `redirectTo`, `children` or `loadChildren`). `redirectTo` cannot be combined
  with `canActivate`/`canMatch` on the same route (same file), which is why the redirects are
  separate child routes.
- `wizardStepGuard` is a `CanActivateFn` (`@angular/router@22.3.0`: `type CanActivateFn = (route,
  state) => MaybeAsync<GuardResult>`, `GuardResult = boolean | UrlTree | RedirectCommand`). It
  allows step 2 only if the wizard state holds step 1 values **for the route's country** that pass
  the same pure validators against the field configuration loaded in this page load. Otherwise it
  returns `new RedirectCommand(router.parseUrl('/<country>/datos'), { replaceUrl: true })`, so the
  blocked address does not stay in the history (AC-19). If the configuration cannot be loaded, it
  redirects to step 1, which shows the load error state.
- Each step is its own history entry: "Continuar" navigates normally (no `replaceUrl`), so the
  browser back action returns to step 1 (US-01-Q-20, AC-20).
- Focus on step change: the arriving step's heading receives focus (step 1 in US-01; step 2 and 3
  in their stories, spec §8).
- Field configuration and countries are fetched once per full page load and kept in memory for
  that page load only (US-01-Q-16); nothing about content is stored across reloads (ADR-0003).

# ADR-0002: Strapi access and security model

## Context and Problem Statement

The browser must read published content (countries and form fields in US-01, plans in US-02,
terms in US-03) from Strapi, and nothing else. We must decide how the browser reaches Strapi
(directly or through a proxy, anonymously or with a token), how the same build learns the API
address in every environment, how we avoid caches that would hide a newly published change, and
how the AC-03 end-to-end test creates content without a write credential ever reaching the

- Bad, because Strapi's CORS (default `origin: '*'`) must be opened to the front-end origin.
- Bad, because caching and method rules can only live in Strapi.

- Good, because no token exists in the read path; nothing to provision.
- Good, because the API address is relative; CORS can be closed.

- Bad, because Strapi's own port still answers the public `find` endpoints (mitigated as above).

  published-only rule is still needed.

- E2E `us-01-security.spec.ts` (AC-27): every browser request to `/api/` is a `GET`, none has an
  `Authorization` header, none contains a step 1 value.
- Check in the same file (an API request from the Node process, no browser): anonymous
  `GET /api/form-fields?status=draft&filters[key][$eq]=email` on Strapi's port returns no `email`
  field; `POST /api/form-fields` through nginx returns `405`.
- E2E `us-01-config-change.spec.ts` (AC-03) follows the write flow above; review checks that the
  token is created and deleted in Node only.

  `false`; no `Authorization` header and no Strapi host name in `frontend/src`;
  `scripts/scan-secrets.sh` exits 0.

### 1. Direct access with the public role

- Good, because there is no proxy configuration at all.
- Bad, because the browser needs Strapi's absolute address, so the build needs a runtime
  `config.json` fetched before bootstrap (`provideAppInitializer`, present in
  `@angular/core@22.3.0`), a second artefact per environment.
- Bad, because Strapi's CORS (default `origin: '*'`) must be opened to the front-end origin.
- Bad, because caching and method rules can only live in Strapi.

- Good, because no token exists in the read path; nothing to provision.

- Bad, because Strapi's own port still answers the public `find` endpoints (mitigated as above).

  pre-hashed key using its internal hashing, both fragile (D4).

  future ones, and `status=draft` is still accepted; a `custom` token narrows it, but the
  published-only rule is still needed.

  effective access is the same as option 2: the security gain is only on Strapi's direct port.

- Related ADRs: ADR-0001 (which types are per country, and why `country` must be readable),
  ADR-0003 (step 1 values never leave the browser).
- Revisit when: the app gains end-user accounts, content that is not public appears, Strapi's
  port must be reachable from the internet without the proxy, or Strapi adds a permission for
  reading drafts through the content API.

## Decision Drivers

- D1. "Use a front-end strategy to persist the data; a database is not required." (source: Assessment; US-01-BR-08)
- D2. Data kept when going back, in-app and with browser back (US-01-AC-04, US-01-AC-20) and across a reload in the same tab, proposed by US-01-Q-15 (US-01-AC-21).
- D3. Data never crosses countries; opening another country's context discards the previous one (US-01-BR-07, US-01-AC-22, US-01-Q-02).
- D4. Privacy: document number and birth date are personal data (US-01-Q-15; spec §9 security/privacy). Step 1 values are never sent to a server or written to logs (US-01-AC-27, CLAUDE.md §3). Masking in the summary (US-03 story: "The document number is shown partially masked").
- D5. A changed configuration must not resurrect values of removed fields or options (US-01-Q-16, US-01-AC-23).
- D6. Retry after a failed payment keeps the data; a successful payment ends the quote (US-03 story: "Rejected payment", "Successful payment").
- D7. "Use fictitious data only." (source: Assessment). Tests and fixtures use only seed values.

## Considered Options

1. **In memory only** (a signal store, lost on reload).
2. **`sessionStorage`**, one versioned entry, scoped to one country, cleared on country change,
   tab close and successful payment.
3. **`localStorage` with an expiry** (for example 30 minutes), same shape.
4. **Hybrid**: `sessionStorage` for non-sensitive values, document number and birth date in
   memory only.

## Decision Outcome

Chosen option: **"2. sessionStorage"**, because it is the only option that survives a reload in
the same tab (D2) while being deleted by the browser when the tab closes, and its per-tab
partitioning keeps a CO tab and a CL tab from overwriting each other (D3). The privacy cost
(personal data in clear text in the tab's storage) is bounded by the tab lifetime and the
clearing rules below (D4).

### What is decided

**Store and storage key**

- A root-provided `QuoteStore` (signals) is the single owner of the wizard state. Components and
  guards never touch `sessionStorage` directly.
- One `sessionStorage` entry, key `quote-wizard`, value JSON:
  `{ "version": 1, "country": "<code>", "step1": { "values": { "<key>": <value> } }, "plan": … }`.
  `values` holds the **raw editing values** of the form model: strings for `text`, `number`,
  `select` and `date`, booleans for `checkbox`, and `''` for an empty field. An in-progress
  invalid value such as `'2015.5'` is stored as typed. The spec §7.3 typed output (`text` →
  trimmed string, `number` → integer, `select` → option value, `date` → `YYYY-MM-DD`, `checkbox`
  → boolean, unchecked optional checkbox → `false`, empty optional → `null`) is produced only on a
  valid "Continuar"; that typed output is what US-02 and US-03 consume. `plan` is added by US-02
  (an identifier of the chosen plan only, defined in its spec).
- **Not stored**: the field configuration, labels, option labels, plans, prices or terms. They are
  fetched once per full page load (US-01-Q-16, ADR-0001) and later steps read labels from that
  in-memory configuration. This settles the open point in spec §7.3 ("Whether it is stored or
  refetched is a persistence ADR detail"): refetched.
- **Never written to storage**: payment data (US-03), if the simulated payment asks for any. It
  lives only in the payment component's memory.
- No cookies, no `localStorage`, no IndexedDB for wizard data.

**When it is written**

- On every change of a step 1 value, the raw editing values are written (the store writes
  synchronously after updating its signal), so a reload restores exactly what the person typed,
  valid or not. The values are revalidated when shown and on "Continuar" (US-01-Q-16); only a
  valid "Continuar" produces the §7.3 typed output.

**When it is read**

- Once, when the store is created (each full page load). The JSON is validated at the boundary:
  wrong `version`, invalid JSON, a `country` that is not an alpha-2 code, or values of an
  unexpected type → the entry is discarded and a `console.warn` without any value is logged.
- When step 1 renders with the configuration of this page load: values whose key is no longer
  configured are dropped from the state, and a `select` value whose option no longer exists is
  cleared (US-01-AC-23). The pruned state is written back.

**Scope per country (US-01-Q-02)**

- The entry holds at most **one** country. When a supported country's context is entered
  (ADR-0001, `/:country` route) and the stored `country` differs, the entry is deleted before
  step 1 renders. Visiting `/` or an unknown country does not delete it.
- `sessionStorage` is partitioned by origin and by tab (MDN: "partitioned by both origin and
  browser tabs (top-level browsing contexts)"), so two tabs with different countries have
  independent state.

**When it is cleared**

| Event | Effect | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Tab or window closed | Browser deletes it (MDN: "Closing the tab/window ends the session and clears the data in `sessionStorage`.") | Browser |
| Another supported country's context entered | Entry deleted | US-01 (`QuoteStore`, called from the `/:country` route) |
| Successful payment | Entry deleted before the confirmation is shown; the confirmation keeps only the simulated quote number in memory | US-03 |
| Rejected payment | **Nothing** cleared: the person retries with the same data | US-03 |
| Unreadable or wrong-version entry | Entry deleted | US-01 |

**Privacy rules**

- Values are never logged (no `console.*` with values, warnings name keys only), never sent in a
  request (US-01-AC-27), never put in the URL, and never in the document title.
- The full document number is stored, because US-03 masks it **at display time**; the masked form
  is never stored separately.
- No client-side encryption: the key would live in the same JavaScript as the data, so it would
  add complexity without protecting against the realistic threat (script injection in the page).
  The protection is the tab lifetime, the clearing rules and the absence of third-party scripts.
- If `sessionStorage` is unavailable (blocked by the browser, quota exceeded), the store keeps the
  state in memory only and logs one `console.warn`; the wizard still works except across reloads.

### Consequences

- Good, because the person keeps their data across steps, browser back and a reload (D2), and
  after a rejected payment (D6).
- Good, because the data disappears with the tab, with a country switch and after payment (D3, D4).
- Good, because one entry with a version number and boundary validation makes later stories'
  additions (plan) and format changes safe.
- Bad, because the document number and birth date sit in clear text in the tab's storage while
  the tab is open, readable by any script running on the origin and by anyone using the same
  browser tab — mitigation: no third-party scripts, values never logged, cleared on payment and
  country switch; the residual risk is accepted for a quote flow without accounts.
- Bad, because MDN notes the page session "survives over page reloads and restores", so a browser
  that restores a crashed or reopened session may bring the data back — mitigation: accepted;
  the data stays on the same device and profile.
- Bad, because a tab opened from the wizard tab may start with a copy of its storage (MDN: with an
  `opener`, "the `sessionStorage` is initially a copy of the opener's") — mitigation: the app opens
  no new windows; copies are independent afterwards.
- Bad, because writing on every change stores invalid intermediate values — mitigation: they are
  revalidated on display and on "Continuar"; the AC-19 guard validates before step 2.
- Neutral: spec US-01-AC-21 ("Data survives a reload") stays as written; the "memory only"
  rewrite foreseen in the spec does not apply.

### Strongest argument against

The document number and birth date stay in clear text in the tab's storage for as long as the
tab is open, readable by any script running on the origin. MDN states that the page session
"survives over page reloads and restores", so a browser that restores a crashed or reopened
session can bring that personal data back. Option 1 (memory only) avoids all of this: nothing
personal is ever written to the device. Its only cost is that a reload loses the data.

**Why we accept it:** losing everything on a reload, which users do on mobile and after errors,
fails the reload behaviour approved for AC-21 (D2), and the AC-19 guard would send the person
back to an empty step 1. The exposure is limited: no third-party scripts, values are never
logged, the entry is cleared on payment and on country switch, and the data stays on the same
device and browser profile. The residual risk is accepted for a quote flow without accounts.

### Confirmation

- Unit tests `quote-store.spec.ts`: the raw editing values (including an in-progress invalid
  value such as `'2015.5'`) are persisted on every change, and a new store instance restores them
  exactly from `sessionStorage` (AC-21); the §7.3 typed output (AC-18) is produced only on a valid
  "Continuar", never on an invalid one; entering another country deletes the entry and the original
  country is empty afterwards (AC-22); removed keys and options are pruned (AC-23); a corrupted or
  wrong-version entry is discarded with a warning that contains no value; storage unavailable →
  memory fallback.
- E2E `us-01-country-context.spec.ts` (AC-22) and `us-01-security.spec.ts` (AC-27, no value in any
  request).
- Review checklist: only `QuoteStore` references `sessionStorage`; no `localStorage`, cookies or
  IndexedDB for wizard data; no `console.*` call receives a value; US-03 clears the entry on
  successful payment and not on a rejected one.

## Pros and Cons of the Options

### 1. In memory only

- Good, because nothing is written to the device; the strongest privacy option.
- Good, because it is the simplest to implement and test.
- Bad, because a reload, which users do on mobile and after errors, loses everything (fails the
  reload behaviour proposed in US-01-Q-15; AC-21 would be rewritten).
- Bad, because a reload on step 2 or 3 sends the person back to an empty step 1 through the AC-19
  guard.

### 2. `sessionStorage` (chosen)

- Good, because it survives reloads and is cleared by the browser when the tab closes.
- Good, because it is partitioned per tab, so different countries in different tabs do not clash.
- Bad, because personal data is in clear text while the tab is open.
- Bad, because browser session restore can bring it back.

### 3. `localStorage` with an expiry

- Good, because the person could close the tab and come back within the expiry.
- Bad, because the data outlives the tab, so on a shared computer the next person can see it; the
  expiry is only enforced when the app runs again.
- Bad, because `localStorage` is shared by all tabs of the origin: a CO tab and a CL tab would
  overwrite each other's state.

### 4. Hybrid (sensitive values in memory only)

- Good, because the document number and birth date never touch storage.
- Bad, because after a reload the person must re-enter exactly the most tedious fields, and the
  AC-19 guard sends them back to step 1 with a partially filled form; AC-21 would hold only for
  some fields.
- Bad, because which keys are sensitive is decided in code, while editors can add new fields
  (for example a phone number) that would silently be stored.

## More Information

- MDN Web Docs, `Window.sessionStorage`
  (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/sessionStorage), read on 2026-11-20:
  lifetime ("survives over page reloads and restores"; "Closing the tab/window ends the session
  and clears the data"), partitioning by origin and tab, copy from an opener.
- Related ADRs: ADR-0001 (country context and the `/:country` route that triggers the switch),
  ADR-0002 (step 1 values never sent; AC-27), ADR-0004 (forms library, reserved: how the form is
  hydrated from the store).
- Revisit when: the product needs to resume a quote on another day or device (that needs a
  server, out of scope), or real personal data is processed (a privacy review would then be
  required).
- Clarified at HC2 (Felipe Sabogal, 2026-11-20): raw editing values in storage; §7.3 typed output
  only on a valid Continuar.

binding. SPIKE-01 built the same form twice, with Signal Forms and with Reactive Forms
(`FormRecord`), over a shared library-agnostic validation core. This ADR decides which approach
the production step 1 uses, and which parts stay outside the library.

## Decision Drivers

  Strapi configuration, with typed validations" (assessment); spec §9 *Typed validations*
  (configuration parsed at the boundary into a typed model; validators are pure functions with an
  injectable clock).
- **D2. Angular 21+ idioms.** "Angular 21 or later: standalone components, signals, built-in
  control flow (@if, @for), no NgModules" (assessment). Angular is pinned to **22.3.0**
  (`CLAUDE.md` §4).
- **D3. Error visibility and focus.** Errors appear after blur or after a failed "Continuar",
  update while typing once shown, and focus moves to the first invalid field in `sortOrder`
  (US-01-AC-10, US-01-Q-13).
- **D4. Hydration and pruning.** The form shows stored values on entry with no errors
  (US-01-AC-04, AC-20, AC-21); values of keys no longer configured are dropped and stale select
  values cleared (US-01-AC-23, Q-16).
- **D5. Correct empty and number semantics.** Required vs empty (`0` is a value, `''` is empty),
  integer-only numbers (US-01-AC-05, AC-08, Q-12, Q-26).
- **D6. Output shape.** Step 1 hands values to later steps in the §7.3 shape: trimmed text,
  integers, ISO dates, booleans, and `null` for an empty optional field.
- **D7. Accessibility.** Native controls, accessible name, description, required and invalid
  states, error announced once (US-01-AC-25, spec §9).
- **D8. Risk and reversibility.** Library maturity, amount of custom code, and the cost of
  switching later (`adr-madr`: hard-to-reverse decisions).

## Considered Options

1. **Signal Forms** (`@angular/forms/signals`: `form`, `FormField`, `FormRoot`, `validate`,
   `submit`) over the shared validation core.
2. **Reactive Forms** (`FormRecord<FormControl<…>>` with `ReactiveFormsModule`) over the same
   core.
3. **No forms library**: native inputs bound to plain signals (`[value]` / `(input)` /
   `(blur)`), with validation, touched state, submit and focus handled by the shared core and the
   component.

## Decision Outcome

Chosen option: **"Signal Forms over the shared validation core"**. Both libraries met every
SPIKE-01 criterion (11/11 each). The tie-breakers are D2, D3 and D5. Signal Forms keeps state in
signals with no bridges. `submit()` touches every field and `focusBoundControl()` moves focus
(D3), so neither needs a DOM lookup or an extra call. With a string model, number inputs had no
accessor surprises (D5). The Reactive Forms adapter needed `normalise()` to fix a real
functional bug: `NumberValueAccessor` wrote a number into a control declared as string, and a
valid year was read as empty. Its one typing advantage (no casts in templates) does not help D1,
because the typed contract lives in the parsed `FieldConfig` and the pure validators, not in
the form model.

### What is decided

- **Library and version:** `@angular/forms/signals` from `@angular/forms` 22.3.0 (pinned, as all
  `@angular/*`, by `CLAUDE.md` §4). The step 1 page does not import `ReactiveFormsModule`,
  `FormControl`, `FormGroup`, `FormRecord` or `@angular/forms/signals-compat`.
- **Validation stays in the core, not in the library.** Validation and message resolution are
  pure functions in `field-validators.ts` (`CLAUDE.md` §6). They import nothing from
  `@angular/forms` and get "today" from the injectable clock (US-01-Q-06). Each field gets
  exactly one `validate()` that calls the shared function and returns
  `{ kind: 'custom', message }`. Signal Forms built-in validators (`required()`, `min()`,
  `pattern()`, …) are not used. The rule order, the empty-optional skip (Q-26) and the message
  priority (Q-04) are configuration semantics, and keeping them in one function keeps this
  decision reversible (D8).
- **Editing model:** `Record<string, string | boolean>`. `text`, `number`, `select` and `date`
  hold strings (`''` = empty); `checkbox` holds a boolean. The model never holds `null`. This
  deliberately differs from the vendored skill's "use `0` for numbers": `0` is a valid value, so
  it cannot mean empty (D5, AC-08). `number` fields use a native `<input type="number">` bound to
  the string model, and integer-only is a validator rule (Q-12).
- **Output mapping:** the §7.3 values come from a pure `toOutput(configs, model)`: trimmed text,
  integer, option value, ISO date, boolean, and `null` for an empty optional field. The output is
  never read back into the form model; hydration goes through `hydrate()`.
- **Hydration and pruning:** the model is created from `hydrate(configs, storedValues)`, which
  keeps only configured keys and converts stored values to the editing model, **before** `form()`
  is called. Signal Forms does not drop unknown keys by itself (SPIKE-01 row g). Clearing a stale
  select value and writing the pruned state back belong to the store (ADR-0003).
- **Lifecycle:** the form is built once per configuration load, in the injection context of the
  component that owns it (a field initialiser of a form component created when the configuration
  is ready). `form()` is not called inside `computed()`, because it creates an effect
  (`NG0602`). A different configuration (another country) means a new component instance, not a
  rebuilt form inside a live one.
- **Error visibility:** an error is shown when `touched() && invalid()`, and only the first
  message (the core already resolves one message per field). "Continuar" calls `submit()` (or
  uses `FormRoot` with `submission` options). `submit()` marks every field as touched.
- **Focus on a failed attempt:** in `onInvalid`, focus the first invalid field in the
  configuration's `sortOrder` with `focusBoundControl()`.
- **Typing at the template boundary:** the runtime union `string | boolean` does not compile
  against native controls (SPIKE-01, *Typing*). Two narrowing accessors (`FieldTree<string>`
  and `FieldTree<boolean>`), selected by the field `type` in a static `@switch`, are the only
  casts allowed. They live in the step 1 form component and nowhere else.
- **Accessibility attributes** (`aria-invalid`, `aria-describedby`, `aria-required`, error
  element) are bound explicitly in the template, as in the spike. `provideSignalFormsConfig` is
  not relied on unless a later review shows it covers AC-25.

### Consequences

- Good, because the form state is signals end to end (D2): `valid()`, `touched()`, `errors()`
  feed the template and the wizard store with no `toSignal` or `valueChanges` bridges.
- Good, because blur and failed-submit visibility share one condition, and focus uses a library
  API instead of DOM queries by id (D3). The spike's sensitivity check proves the test catches its
  removal.
- Good, because the string editing model avoids the accessor writing `number | null` into a
  string-typed state (D5). Integer-only and required-vs-empty stay explicit, testable rules.
- Good, because the validation core is library-agnostic (209 lines in the spike) and is
  unit-tested without Angular forms. Switching library later means rewriting one adapter of
  about 110 lines plus its template, not the rules (D8).
- Bad, because Signal Forms has been public API only since **22.0.0 (2026-06-03)**, about five
  and a half months, and the `forms` scope has had **39** fix, perf or feat entries between
  22.0.0 and 22.3.0 in the CHANGELOG. Mitigation: pinned 22.3.0; the parts we use are small
  (`form`, `validate`, `submit`, `FormField`, `FormRoot`, `focusBoundControl`), all
  `@publicApi 22.0`; no async validators, no `debounce`, no `hidden`/`disabled` logic; validation
  semantics live outside the library.
- Bad, because the runtime model loses static typing in templates and needs two casts. A cast
  cannot catch a mismatch between a field's `type` and the accessor used. Mitigation: the
  accessor is picked in the same `@switch` branch that renders the control; a component test
  renders every field type and asserts the DOM value, and the review checklist rejects other
  casts on form fields.
- Bad, because an unknown key on the field tree compiles but throws at runtime
  (`TypeError: f.<key> is not a function`). Mitigation: the template iterates only over the
  parsed configuration, from which the model is built; no code indexes the tree by a literal key.
- Bad, because all SPIKE-01 evidence comes from jsdom: real focus, native date and number UI,
  `badInput` and screen reader announcements are unverified. Under the HTML value sanitisation
  rule for `type=number`, unparseable input such as `1e` makes `element.value` `''`, so it
  would show the "required" message rather than the format message. The spike did not exercise
  this. Mitigation: the CO e2e (US-01-T-11) exercises keyboard and
  validation in a real browser; the HC3 manual pass includes a screen reader check (spec §9).
- Neutral: Reactive Forms remains fully supported in 22.3.0 (`FormRecord` and
  `ReactiveFormsModule` are `@publicApi`, not deprecated). Later stories may revisit if a form
  needs something Signal Forms lacks.

### Strongest argument against

Signal Forms has been public API only since 22.0.0, about five and a half months, with 39
forms-scope fix, perf or feat entries through 22.3.0. All SPIKE-01 evidence comes from jsdom, not
a real browser. For a form built at runtime its typing benefit largely disappears: the template
needed casts, and an unknown key compiles but throws at runtime. Reactive Forms `FormRecord` is
the long-established path for runtime-keyed forms; in the spike it compiled with no casts, and
`setValue` throws on stale keys.

**Why we accept it:** only APIs tagged `@publicApi 22.0` are used, with no async validators,
`debounce` or `hidden`/`disabled` logic, on a pinned 22.3.0. Validation semantics live outside
the library, so switching to Reactive Forms means rewriting one adapter of about 110 lines plus
its template, not the rules (D8). The Reactive adapter was not free of risk either: it needed
`normalise()` to fix a real bug where `NumberValueAccessor` wrote `number | null` into a
string-typed control (D5). The real-browser gap is covered by the CO e2e (US-01-T-11) and the
HC3 screen reader check.

- **Tests (test-engineer, step 3):** component tests in `quote-form-page.spec.ts` for
  US-01-AC-10 (no errors on entry; error after blur; all errors and focus on the first invalid
  field in `sortOrder` after a failed "Continuar", checked through `document.activeElement`),
  US-01-AC-04 / AC-23 (hydrated values shown, pristine, stale key dropped, stale select shows the
  prompt) and US-01-AC-05 (`2015.5` invalid). Unit tests of `toOutput` for every §7.3 mapping.
- **Static checks (code-reviewer, step 6):**
  `grep -rnE "ReactiveFormsModule|FormControl|FormGroup|FormRecord|signals-compat" frontend/src/app`
  returns nothing. `field-validators.ts` imports nothing from `@angular/forms`. `form(` does not
  appear inside a `computed(`. The only `as unknown as FieldTree` casts are the two accessors.
- **Version:** `frontend/package.json` pins `@angular/forms` to exactly `22.3.0`.

## Pros and Cons of the Options

### 1. Signal Forms over the shared validation core

SPIKE-01 adapter: `signal-forms/dynamic-form-signal.ts` + `.html` (111 lines).

- Good, because it is the signal-native forms API, and Angular's own guide says "Signal Forms
  work best in new applications built with signals" (angular.dev Signal Forms overview, read
  2026-11-20). That matches D2.
- Good, because `submit()` touches the whole tree (verified in `@angular/forms@22.3.0`
  `fesm2022/_validation_errors-chunk.mjs`, `submit` calls `node.markAsTouched()`), and
  `FieldState.focusBoundControl()` is public API. Together they cover D3 with no custom
  plumbing (SPIKE-01 rows h, i).
- Good, because a string model on number and date inputs reads `element.value` with no
  conversion. Required-vs-empty and integer-only worked with no workaround (row a).
- Good, because hydration is "build the model, then the form", and the output maps cleanly to
  §7.3 with a non-null model (rows f, j; D4, D6).
- Bad, because it has been public for about 5.5 months, with steady fixes in 22.x (see
  *Consequences*).
- Bad, because the runtime union does not compile against native controls, so two casts are
  needed (row e).
- Bad, because `form()` creates an effect: it needs an injection context and cannot run inside
  `computed()` (`NG0602`).
- Bad, because the model does not prune unknown keys. Pruning must happen before the model is
  built (row g).

### 2. Reactive Forms (`FormRecord`) over the shared validation core

SPIKE-01 adapter: `reactive-forms/dynamic-form-reactive.ts` + `.html` (112 lines).

- Good, because `FormRecord` is the long-established, documented path for forms keyed at
  runtime, and it is fully supported and not deprecated in 22.3.0 (`@publicApi` in
  `types/forms.d.ts`).
- Good, because `[formControl]` accepts `FormControl<string | boolean>` with **no casts**, and
  `controls[key]` / `get(key)` give an honest `undefined` / `null` for unknown keys (row e).
- Good, because `FormGroup.setValue` throws on extra keys, a built-in guard against stale
  stored keys (row g).
- Good, because it works with standalone components (`ReactiveFormsModule` is imported into the
  component; we write no NgModule), so D2's "no NgModules" is met.
- Bad, because `NumberValueAccessor` writes `number | null` into a control declared as
  `string | boolean`, and `nonNullable` does not prevent it. In the spike this made a valid year
  read as empty until `normalise()` was added to both the validator input and the output mapping
  (row a; D5). The declared type misdescribes the runtime value.
- Bad, because a failed submit touches nothing unless `markAllAsTouched()` is called, and there
  is no focus API, so focus needs a DOM lookup by id (rows h, i; D3).
- Bad, because control state (`touched`, `valid`) is not signals. A signals-based wizard needs
  bridges, or relies on template events to re-render under zoneless change detection (D2).

### 3. No forms library: native inputs bound to plain signals

Not built in SPIKE-01. Assessed from the shared core, which already does all parsing,
validation, hydration and output mapping without any forms API.

- Good, because there is no adapter mismatch at all: each input binds `[value]` to a
  `string`/`boolean` signal and writes `element.value` / `element.checked` back. There are no
  casts and no value accessors.
- Good, because it has the smallest dependency surface. Nothing changes if a forms API changes
  in a later Angular release (D8).
- Good, because every behaviour (touched-on-blur, show-all-on-submit, focus) is explicit code
  that the tests read directly.
- Bad, because it re-implements what both libraries already provide: per-field touched state,
  submit handling, invalid aggregation, and focus by DOM lookup. That is more custom code to
  test and review (D3, D8).
- Bad, because there is no spike evidence for it. Its D3/D7 behaviour would be unproven until
  the production tests run.
- Bad, because a hand-rolled form in an assessment that grades "technical quality" on
  Angular 21+ idioms is a weaker signal than using the framework's forms API (D2).

## More Information

- **Spike:** [docs/spikes/SPIKE-01-forms.md](../docs/spikes/SPIKE-01-forms.md). Code on branch
  `spike/01-forms`, commit `be9ae50` (never merged):
  <https://github.com/FelipeSuarez25/multicountry-car-insurance/tree/spike/01-forms/spikes/spike-01-forms>.
  38/38 tests passed, re-run independently by the orchestrator with `@angular/core` and
  `@angular/forms` 22.3.0.
- **Verified facts (2026-11-20):**
  - npm `@angular/forms` dist-tag `latest` = `22.3.0`, published 2026-11-18; `22.0.0` published
    2026-06-03 (`npm view @angular/forms time`).
  - angular/angular `CHANGELOG.md`, release **22.0.0 (2026-06-03)**, forms: commit
    [`7745365910`](https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/7745365910771d97c91e9b640c2c26a99bfa5a6d)
    "graduate signal forms APIs to public API". It matches EVAL-001, criterion 5
    (`docs/skills/third-party-evaluation.md`).
  - Published `@angular/forms@22.3.0` typings (`npm pack` into a temp dir): `form`, `submit`,
    `FormField`, `FormRoot`, `validate`, `FieldState` (which declares `focusBoundControl`),
    `FormSubmitOptions` (`onInvalid`, `ignoreValidators`) and `provideSignalFormsConfig` are
    tagged `@publicApi 22.0`. The `@experimental` items are WebMCP-related
    (`experimentalWebMcpTool`, `provideExperimentalWebMcpForms`), which we do not use.
    `FormRecord`, `ReactiveFormsModule` and `NumberValueAccessor` are `@publicApi` with no class
    deprecation.
  - CHANGELOG `forms` scope between 22.0.0 and 22.3.0: 39 fix, perf or feat entries.
  - angular.dev Signal Forms overview (unversioned page, read 2026-11-20): "Signal Forms work
    best in new applications built with signals." "If you're working with an existing
    application that uses reactive forms, reactive forms remain a solid choice."
- **Third-party skill conflict (`CLAUDE.md` §1, §5):** the vendored `signal-forms.md` says
  "MUST use Signal Forms" and "Use 0 for numbers, NOT null". This ADR reaches Signal Forms on
  its own drivers, not because of the skill. It **departs** from the skill on number fields
  (string model, `''` for empty) and does not use the skill's built-in validators for
  config-driven rules.
- **Related ADRs:** ADR-0001 (routes; the step 1 page at `/:country/datos`), ADR-0003 (the
  store that provides `storedValues`, prunes stale keys and options, and receives `toOutput`).
- **Revisit when:** a real-browser test or the HC3 pass shows focus, number or date behaviour
  that Signal Forms cannot meet; an Angular upgrade (which needs its own ADR, `CLAUDE.md` §4)
  changes a Signal Forms API we use; or a later story needs dynamic form features (arrays,
  cross-field rules) that the spike did not cover.
